ANDREW HINZ’S REQUEST FOR REHEARING ON FEDERAL INTERCONNECTION
  TARIFFS FOR LARGE LOADS CO-LOCATED AT GENERATING FACILITIES

        The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) December 18, 2025 Order in EL25-

49 Etal will cause unjust and unreasonable rates because:

             1. The Order ignores the costs to ratepayers (wholesale, retail, interstate, intrastate)

                 that will result from just-retired generating facilities, soon-to-retire generating

                 facilities, or new state-sited generating facilities that increase CH4 and/or CO2

                 emissions, because those state-sited generating facilities and their increased

                 emissions will increase cost burdens on ratepayers outside of their states

                 (increased demand and costs for fuel supplies and climate change adaption) for

                 economic benefits limited to the siting states.

             2. The Order does not explicitly open access to the directed PJM tariff to any and all

                 wholesale generating facilities or proposed generating facilities or Co-Located

                 customer types.

             3. The Order does not require that States and Indigenous Tribes or Nations have the

                 ability to approve or reject any terms of any interconnection under any such tariff,

                 regardless of whether they have previously sited a generation facility applying for

                 the tariff.

Request for Rehearing

Federal Tariffs for Large Loads Co-Located at Generating Facilities 1
              4. The Order does not require fuel supply provisions for generating facilities using

                 such tariffs to prevent fuel supply constraints from exacerbating costs to all

                 ratepayers (wholesale, retail, interstate, intrastate) in all or several states resulting

                 from congested grids during peak demand or public emergency responses,

                 regardless of whether those ratepayers receive any benefit from the Co-Location

                 customers of those generating facilities.

        Because of the deficiencies noted above, FERC must Rehear its December 18, 2025

Order in EL25-49. As an alternative, FERC may remedy the deficiencies noted above by

amending the December 18, 2025 Order in EL25-49 as follows:

              (D) Paper hearing procedures are established to evaluate the rates, terms, and conditions of
    the interim, non-firm transmission service, Firm Contract Demand transmission service, and Non-
    Firm Contract Demand transmission service. Those paper hearing procedures will seek comment on
    the following so the Commission can preclude unjust and unreasonable rates resulting from
    approved Tariffs for Large Loads Co-Located at Generating Facilities: emissions-related costs to all
    ratepayers, removal of barriers to such tariffs for all existing and proposed generating facilities and
    all existing and proposed large-load customers (beyond datacenters, including municipal microgrids
    etc.), state authority approving over each tariff agreement regardless of the state siting status of the
    applying generating facility, unintended peak usage and public emergency response rate impacts to
    all ratepayers due to fuel market supply constraints associated with co-located generating facilities
    for large load customers.


Dated: February 8, 2026                              Respectfully submitted,

                                                     Andrew Hinz
